sources.name: Descript Help: Edit like a doc
Descript Help: Create a new project

caption:
Descript turns your video into a transcript, and deleting words in the text cuts them from the video.
It can also strip out filler words and take edit requests in a chat with its AI co-editor, Underlord.
The free plan gives you 60 media minutes a month and exports at 720p with a watermark.

Would you rather edit a video like a document?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Descript Help Center · Photo: Descript
threads_text: Descript lets you edit a video by deleting words from its transcript, and the cut happens in the video too. The free plan has 60 media minutes a month and 720p exports with a watermark, paid plans start at $16 a month billed yearly. Would you edit video this way?

slides.headline: How to use *Descript*: edit your video by deleting words from the transcript

slides.heading: 1. Cut video by *deleting text*
paras: Descript transcribes your file and links the text to the media. Select words and press Delete to cut them from both.
Changed your mind? Right click the edit and choose Restore removed media.

slides.heading: 2. Remove *filler words* in bulk
paras: In the AI Tools panel, choose Remove filler words to find every um and uh in the script.
Turn on Avoid harsh cuts to skip the ones that would sound choppy. English only.

slides.heading: 3. Ask *Underlord* to edit
paras: Underlord is Descript's AI co-editor, in beta. Ask it for captions, short clips or a translation.
Every prompt uses AI credits, and Descript warns it can overpromise. Check its work.

slides.heading: 4. Know the *limits*
paras: Free gives 60 media minutes a month and 720p exports with a watermark.
Hobbyist is $16 a month billed yearly for 10 media hours and 1080p. Creator adds 4K.

slides.hook: Follow for AI tool guides that show the limits before you pay.

site_article.headline: How to use Descript to edit video by editing text
site_article.dek: Descript turns your recording into a transcript that stays linked to the video, so cutting words cuts the footage. Here is the workflow, the AI tools, and what each plan really includes.
site_article.summary: Descript is a video and audio editor that transcribes your media and lets you edit it by editing the text. The free plan includes 60 media minutes a month and 720p exports with a watermark, and paid plans start at $16 a month billed annually.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Descript to edit video by editing text
site_article.seo_description: How to use Descript step by step: create a project, cut video by deleting transcript text, remove filler words, use Underlord, and compare the plans.
site_article.answer_summary: Create a project, add your video so Descript transcribes it, then select words in the script and press Delete to cut them from the video too. Filler word removal sits in the AI Tools panel, and the free plan covers 60 media minutes a month.
site_article.hero_alt: Descript promotional banner showing the video editor interface.

paragraphs.text: Descript is a video and audio editor that transcribes your recording and keeps the transcript linked to the media, according to its help center. If you want to know how to use Descript, the short version is this: add a video, let it transcribe, then delete, move and fix words in the script, and the video changes with them. You can start for free.

Zapier's tutorial on Descript sums up the pitch: if you can edit a document, you can edit a video in it. That is mostly true for talking videos, podcasts and interviews, where the words carry the edit. For footage with little speech, the transcript has less to offer.
How to start a Descript project

paragraphs.title: 1. Create a new project
paragraphs.text: From your drive, click New project in the top right corner and choose the type of project. If a project is already open, click the menu icon in the top left corner and pick File, then New, then Project. New projects save to your personal private workspace unless you are on an Enterprise plan and choose a different one.

paragraphs.title: 2. Add your media
paragraphs.text: Upload a video, audio or image file from your computer, or bring files in from another project, your drive's Media Library, Zoom cloud recordings or, in Descript for Web only, Google Drive. Descript says it handles most common audio, video and image types, plus PDF slide decks, where each slide becomes its own layer. The Activity panel shows upload progress, and canceled uploads are not charged media minutes.

paragraphs.title: 3. Put the file in the script
paragraphs.text: Uploaded files appear under Files in the Project panel on the right. When you add a file to the script, Descript transcribes the speech so you can edit by text. You can also use files as timeline layers for B-roll, visuals or background music.
How to edit video by editing the transcript

paragraphs.title: 4. Delete words to cut the video
paragraphs.text: Select text in the script and press Delete or Backspace. The words disappear from the transcript and the matching audio and video disappear with them. Editing is non-destructive: to bring something back, right click the edit boundary and choose Restore removed media.

paragraphs.title: 5. Move sections with cut and paste
paragraphs.text: Cut a passage with Command X on a Mac or Ctrl X on Windows, click where it should go and paste with Command V or Ctrl V. The media moves with the text. Copy instead of cut if you want to duplicate a section.

paragraphs.title: 6. Fix the transcript
paragraphs.text: Use Correct your transcript to fix typos, wrong words and speaker labels. If you need precise timing, for captions or sync fixes, the wordbar lets you adjust where each word starts and ends. Ignore strikes through text but keeps it visible in the script, and Remove from transcript hides text from the script, captions and exported transcripts while leaving the media in place.

To mark a laugh, a cough or another sound that is not speech, type an opening parenthesis, the note and a closing parenthesis. Inline notes show up in exported transcripts. For feedback to a teammate, use comments instead.
How to remove filler words in Descript

paragraphs.title: 7. Run Remove filler words
paragraphs.text: Open the AI Tools panel in the right sidebar and choose Remove filler words. A sidebar lists each detected filler word with a timestamp, and the words are underlined in light blue in the script. Preview them, then choose Delete, Delete and replace with gap to keep the timing, Ignore, or Remove from transcript.

Turn on Avoid harsh cuts before you apply the removal. Descript then skips filler words it cannot remove without clipping the words around them. Filler word detection works only on English transcripts and uses AI credits on current plans. To clean only part of a video, duplicate that section to a new composition, run the tool there and paste the result back.
How to use Underlord, the AI co-editor

Underlord is Descript's AI co-editor, still labeled beta. You open it from its icon in the right sidebar of any project and type requests, such as adding captions, cutting clips, translating, adding zooms and fades or applying Studio Sound at a set intensity. The model selector near the bottom of the chat lets you pick a model, and premium models need a paid plan.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: Find short clips for social
paragraphs.text: Find the best 60 to 90 second moments in this video and turn each one into a vertical clip for social media.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Add styled captions
paragraphs.text: Add social style captions to this video in [your brand color], with a bold font and a dark background behind the text.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Clean up the audio
paragraphs.text: Apply Studio Sound at [intensity] to the speaker track and lower the other audio so the speech stands out.

Each Underlord prompt uses AI credits, and when it runs a tool you pay for both the reasoning and the tool, with costs that vary between runs of the same prompt, according to the help center. Descript also says plainly that Underlord can overpromise, make wrong assumptions or try workflows it cannot finish, and that it works best when you check its output as you go.
Descript plans and limits

The Free plan costs nothing and includes 60 media minutes a month, 100 one time AI credits and 720p exports with a watermark, according to the pricing page. Hobbyist is $16 per person a month billed annually or $24 monthly, with 10 media hours, 400 AI credits a month and 1080p export. Creator is $24 billed annually or $35 monthly, with 30 media hours, 800 credits and 4K export. Business is $50 billed annually or $65 monthly, with 40 media hours and 1,500 credits. Sonix lists the same prices and allowances in its review.

Studio Sound, Remove Filler Words and Underlord are limited on the Free plan and included on the paid ones. Transcription covers 25 languages on every plan. Cloud storage runs from 5GB on Free to 2TB on Business.
What Descript is bad at

Transcripts are not perfect. Zapier's tutorial says the transcript is fairly accurate but sometimes gets things wrong. Sonix, a competing transcription company, estimates accuracy at about 92 to 95 percent for clean single speaker English, lower with heavy accents or three or more speakers, and says Descript is designed for recordings under 60 minutes. Sonix also says AI credits do not roll over, and that heavy use of Studio Sound and Underlord can use up the Creator plan's 800 credits.

Descript is at its best on spoken content: podcasts, interviews, tutorials and talking head videos. The text editing alone saves real time, and it works on the free plan. The weak spots are the meters. Media minutes and AI credits both run out, Underlord can burn credits on retries, and filler word removal is English only. Read the transcript before you cut, do simple trims by hand, and save the AI tools for jobs that would take you longer.
